title.en: Describe the discovery of the electron, proton and neutron
Use Z and A to count protons, neutrons and electrons

say.en: Dalton thought atoms could not be broken. Then a glowing tube, a drop of oil and a sheet of gold foil showed that an atom has electrons, protons and a tiny heavy nucleus. In this lesson: Describe the discovery of the electron, proton and neutron.
Explain Thomson's and Rutherford's models.
Use Z and A to count protons, neutrons and electrons.

body.en: Cathode ray tube experiments showed negatively charged *particles*, electrons, in all atoms. J. J. Thomson measured their charge-to-mass ratio, $e/m_e$ = 1.758820 × 10$^{11}$ C kg$^{-1}$, and Millikan’s oil-drop experiment gave the charge, 1.602 × 10$^{-19}$ C, so $m_e$ = 9.1094 × 10$^{-31}$ kg. Canal rays led to the proton, and in 1932 Chadwick discovered the neutral neutron by bombarding beryllium with α-particles.
body.kn: ಕ್ಯಾಥೋಡ್ ಕಿರಣಗಳಿಂದ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್, ಕ್ಯಾನಲ್ ಕಿರಣಗಳಿಂದ ಪ್ರೋಟಾನ್ ಪತ್ತೆಯಾದವು. 1932ರಲ್ಲಿ ಚಾಡ್ವಿಕ್ ನ್ಯೂಟ್ರಾನ್ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿದರು.

narration.en: Cathode rays revealed the electron, Thomson measured its charge to mass ratio, and Millikan measured its charge. Canal rays led to the proton, and Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932.
narration.kn: ಕ್ಯಾಥೋಡ್ ಕಿರಣಗಳಿಂದ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್, ಕ್ಯಾನಲ್ ಕಿರಣಗಳಿಂದ ಪ್ರೋಟಾನ್ ಪತ್ತೆಯಾದವು. 1932ರಲ್ಲಿ ಚಾಡ್ವಿಕ್ ನ್ಯೂಟ್ರಾನ್ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿದರು.

Neutron: no charge, 1.6749 times 10 to the power minus 27 kilograms.

title.en: From plum pudding to the nucleus

say.en: Thomson pictured the atom as a sphere of positive charge with electrons stuck in it, like plums in a pudding.
Rutherford fired alpha particles at thin gold foil. Most went straight through, a few were deflected, and about one in twenty thousand bounced back.
So nearly all the mass and all the positive charge sit in a tiny nucleus, with electrons moving around it at a distance.
We write an atom as X with the mass number A on top and the atomic number Z below. Neutrons are A minus Z.
Isotopes have the same Z but different A, like protium, deuterium and tritium. Isobars have the same A but different Z, like argon-40 and calcium-40.
From plum pudding to the nucleus.

narration.en: Alpha particles fly at a gold nucleus. Most pass far from it and go almost straight; the few that come close are pushed away at large angles, and a head-on one bounces back. In the plum-pudding model nothing would bounce back.
narration.kn: ಆಲ್ಫಾ ಕಣಗಳು ಚಿನ್ನದ ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯಸ್ ಕಡೆ ಹಾರುತ್ತವೆ. ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನವು ದೂರದಿಂದ ಬಹುತೇಕ ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಹೋಗುತ್ತವೆ; ಹತ್ತಿರ ಬಂದ ಕೆಲವು ದೊಡ್ಡ ಕೋನದಲ್ಲಿ ತಿರುಗುತ್ತವೆ, ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಬಂದದ್ದು ಹಿಂತಿರುಗುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: *Thomson* pictured the atom as a sphere of positive charge with electrons embedded in it (the plum-pudding model). In Rutherford's gold-foil experiment most α-particles passed straight through, a few were deflected, and about 1 in 20 000 bounced back. So nearly all the mass and all the positive charge sit in a tiny nucleus, with electrons moving around it. Atomic number Z = number of protons; mass number A = protons + neutrons. Isotopes have the same Z but different A; isobars have the same A but different Z.
body.kn: ರುದರ್‌ಫೋರ್ಡ್ ಪ್ರಯೋಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ α-ಕಣಗಳು ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಹಾದುಹೋದವು, ಕೆಲವು ಮಾತ್ರ ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಬಂದವು. ಹೀಗಾಗಿ ಪರಮಾಣುವಿನ ರಾಶಿ ಮತ್ತು ಧನ ಆವೇಶ ಸಣ್ಣ ಬೀಜಕೇಂದ್ರದಲ್ಲಿದೆ. ಸಮಸ್ಥಾನಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಒಂದೇ Z, ಬೇರೆ A.

heading.en: Subatomic Particles and Early Atomic Models

tagline.en: Cathode rays and the electron, e/m and Millikan's charge, protons and neutrons, Thomson's and Rutherford's models, atomic number, mass number, isotopes and isobars, and why Rutherford's model failed.

myth.en: Rutherford's model is complete: electrons simply orbit the nucleus like planets, so the atom is stable.

truth.en: By classical electromagnetic theory, an electron moving in a circle is accelerating and must radiate energy, so it would spiral into the nucleus. Rutherford's model cannot explain the stability of atoms, nor the energies and arrangement of electrons. Planets are neutral and do not radiate, so the analogy feels safe. Charged particles do radiate when accelerated, and that is the weakness that led to Bohr's model.

narration.en: Many people think: Rutherford's model is complete: electrons simply orbit the nucleus like planets, so the atom is stable. Actually: By classical electromagnetic theory, an electron moving in a circle is accelerating and must radiate energy, so it would spiral into the nucleus. Rutherford's model cannot explain the stability of atoms, nor the energies and arrangement of electrons. Planets are neutral and do not radiate, so the analogy feels safe.
